channel.title: NBC Sports Fantasy Football News
channel.description: Latest player news and analysis for fantasy football from NBC Sports.

item.title: Giants signed RB Gregory Desrosiers off the Chargers’ practice squad.
item.description: The first-year UDFA rushed for 166 yards on 23 carries in the preseason for the Chargers, adding one touchdown and one eight-yard reception. We’d be surprised if he got real run in this backfield but at least he has the bye week to acclimate.-Rivers McCown

item.title: Giants GM Joe Schoen said the Giants will place Tyrone Tracy (hamstring) on injured reserve.
item.description: Well that sorts out the Giants backfield for the short term. Devin Singletary will take over as the primary passing down back behind Cam Skattebo and should be a usable FLEX play going forward. Tracy will miss the next four weeks after going down with the hamstring injury in the second quarter of New York’s win over the Texans in Week 7. Schoen indicated this isn’t a season-ender for Tracy.-Rivers McCown

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports the Colts could trade Josh Downs.
item.description: Schefter listed out DeForest Buckner, Grover Stewart, and Downs as players that could potentially be on the move as the Colts continue what from all outside appearances looks to be a fire sale. He thinks Buckner will be the next player on the move and likely go for less than Quenton Nelson. Downs certainly hasn’t impressed with his opportunity this season, but he’s a valuable receiver and Indianapolis didn’t exactly but him in an ideal scenario with Alec Pierce hurt and Keenan Allen playing alongside him while Daniel Jones struggles to regain his 2025 form.-Rivers McCown

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Colts ownership does not want to trade Jonathan Taylor.
item.description: Schefter said that if he had to guess today, he doesn’t think the Colts will part with Taylor. There are still a few weeks ahead of the trade deadline, and it’s certainly possible that a team bowls them over with an offer. This is going to remain a topic of conversation until the deadline passes. But it is worth noting that ownership believes in Taylor as a difference-maker.-Rivers McCown

item.title: Bears signed RB Zavier Scott to their active roster from the practice squad.
item.description: The Bears had run out of elevations with him, so had to sign him to the roster to have him active for Week 8. Scott has played 46 special teams snaps and 0 offensive snaps so far and does not need to be rostered for fantasy purposes. It’s hard to not read this as bad news about Kyle Monangai’s health in the short term, but we’re trying.-Rivers McCown

item.title: Bengals placed Erick All (knee) on injured reserve.
item.description: Per NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport, this is believed to be a third torn ACL. Obviously it’s not good news that All, who missed a season-and-a-half the last time he damaged his knee, is dealing with another long-term knee injury. He’s in the third year of a four-year rookie contract but his NFL future looks to be in doubt.-Rivers McCown

item.title: 49ers general manager John Lynch said the team would continue starting Eddy Pineiro after the team’s Week 7 bye.
item.description: Lynch in a Tuesday interview acknowledged Pineiro is “going through a rough patch” but committed to sticking with him for now. “We have a lot of belief in Eddie,” Lynch added. “He has had a tough run early this year, but we extended Eddie for his body of work with us but then throughout the history of his career.” Pineiro has missed three of his nine field goal tries on the season and four of his 25 extra point attempts. Pineiro, who made 96 percent of his field goal tries in 2025, will have at least a couple more games before the Niners brings in kicker competition.-Denny Carter

item.title: Seahawks acquired Quenten Nelson from the Colts in exchange for a 2027 third-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick.
item.description: With the Colts’ season all but over, the team could trade away a series of key player as they look toward a total tear down/rebuild scenario following the 2026 season. That includes Nelson, an eight-time Pro Bowler who now has a chance to compete for a title now that he’s out of Indianapolis. Nelson will join a Seattle offensive line that ranks 21st in pass blocking win rate and 27th in run blocking win rate. His addition should be a boon for Sam Darnold and the Seahawks’ pass catchers.-Denny Carter

item.title: The Athletic’s Alec Lewis believes Kyler Murray is still “acclimating to the [Vikings’] progression-based passing game.”
item.description: Minnesota’s offensive ineptitude has reached stunning levels in recent weeks, including last Sunday against the Colts, when Murray had 150 yards and a touchdown while completing 58 percent of his pass attempts. “We’ll continue to get better,” Murray said Sunday night. “I know we will. I know we keep saying that, but I felt like we moved the ball well (against the Colts). We’ve just got to put the ball in the end zone.” The Vikings, who rank 25th in pass rate over expected this season, have operated conservatively on offense while their defense dismantles opponents week in and week out. As Lewis pointed out, the 2026 Vikings are the first team in a century to win five straight games with five or fewer TDs over that span. Murray through Week 7 ranks 28th out of 40 qualifying QBs in EPA per pass attempt and 33rd in fantasy points per drop back.-Denny Carter

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Vega Ioane suffered an MCL injury and will miss time.
item.description: Ioane went down with a knee injury on Sunday against the Bengals and did not return to the game. Though Rapoport said the injury is not considered long term, Ioane — an impressive rookie — will be sidelined for a while. Baltimore’s offensive line ranks 20th in pass block win rate and 19th in run block win rate, according to ESPN.-Denny Carter
